title: Micro-playbook: retrieval + context recipes (personal)
content:
Quick, messy notes from sprint + workshop skims. Intended as my personal micro-playbook for experiments and small fixes to try on customer workloads. Lots of heuristics, not canonical.

Goals
- reduce token spend for long-context RAG while preserving answer fidelity
- prioritize low-latency hits for short queries, fall back to expensive retrieval for long ones

Useful heuristics (practical)
1) Query bucketing: if query length < 40 tokens -> fast-path: embed+k=5 cheap index (64-d dim), else -> robust-path: k=12 dense+BM25 hybrid
2) Prefix pruning: for user chats, strip signatures/long quoted text before embedding (save 15-40% tokens)
3) Soft-fallback: if top-1 doc similarity < 0.26 -> trigger rerank with cross-encoder only on top-8

Prompt templates (cheap-first)
- System: "You are a concise assistant. Use at most 150 tokens for the answer unless user asks for long form. Cite sections like [doc#3:line42]."
- RAG assemble: include only top-3 doc extracts truncated to 400 chars each; add "IF uncertain, say \"I might be wrong\" and ask for clarification" to reduce hallucinations.

Lightweight eval plan
- Eval set: 300 user-support queries from last 90 days (sample stratified by length)
- Metrics: exact match on KB pointers, F1 for answer, cost-per-query (hosted billing)
- A/B ideas: k=5 cheap vs k=12 hybrid, with cross-encoder rerank only on low-sim cases

Immediate experiments (todo)
- run cheap-index k=5 on sample; measure latency and failure modes (JIRA-ENG-1423)
- test prefix-pruning micro-rewrite: measure token savings and change in pointer accuracy
- try cascading reranker: cheap embed -> cross-encoder only when top similarity between 0.18-0.30

Notes-to-self / loose thoughts
- Consider TTL cache keyed by (user_id, fingerprint(query_short_form)) for repeated short queries
- Watch out for cost regressions when enabling cross-encoder on heavy traffic; simulate traffic bursts
- Could add a lightweight classifier to predict whether answer requires >1 doc; train on signal: #docs clicked in support logs

Relevant papers & quick takeaways
- Retro/long-context: useful for archive stitching but heavy for low-latency; prefer selective retrieval + tiny generator for short replies
- Dense+BM25 hybrid: good robustness; if index budget allows, keep both and prefer BM25 when exact phrase match expected

Slack/Git refs
- convo thread: #ops-rag-fastpath (link in linked_artifacts)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playbooks/pull/87 (prototype reranker gating)

Open questions
- How to set similarity thresholds adaptively per-customer? (per-cust calibrator?)
- When to evict cached reprompt outputs vs cached embeddings? (cost vs staleness)

If time: draft a short customer-facing one-pager for CS: "how we keep your RAG fast and cheap" with 3 knobs (k, rerank gating, prefix-prune). Keep it 1 page, visuals later.

End of scratchpad. Revisit after cheap-index run (assigned to Ravi).
